transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I'm really mostly here because my primary care doctor asked me to come. She seems a little concerned that my... well, that my meal planning has gotten a bit too tight lately. But honestly, I think she might be worrying over nothing. I don't want to make a fuss out of it. 

To me, it just feels like I'm being organized. I usually just keep breakfast to a little yogurt, and, you know, I'll skip lunch if I’m busy—which happens a lot with my work—and then I just make sure to have a very measured dinner. It just helps keep the whole day orderly and on track. That makes sense, right? I just like to be efficient and keep things structured... I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or do you consider your weight to be below what's healthy for your height?

Well, I mean... my primary doctor did mention that my weight has drifted down a bit more than she'd like. I guess it has dropped some. But, um, I don't really see it as unhealthy? 

Actually, when I look at the numbers on the scale, I... well, I still find myself thinking that maybe a little lower would just be a cleaner, more manageable number. It's just about feeling comfortable in my own body, you know? I hope that doesn't sound too strange. It's not like I'm trying to be unhealthy or anything, I just like things to be precise. Is that... is that okay?
Do you find yourself being very afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if it's just a small amount?

Oh, "afraid" seems like such a strong word... I don't want to sound dramatic or anything. But, um... I suppose I do get a little, well, anxious about it. 

It’s actually a bit embarrassing to admit, but if I have a normal dinner, or maybe a restaurant meal, and the scale is up even just a single pound the next morning... I do feel this rather sharp panic. It just makes me feel like I’ve completely lost control of my routine. So I just make sure to correct it the next day, just to get the numbers back where they belong. 

It’s really just about maintaining equilibrium and fixing the variance. I hope you don't think that sounds too silly? I just like to keep things balanced.
Do you feel that your sense of self-worth depends very strongly on your body weight or shape?

Well, I... I wouldn't say my whole worth depends on it, no. I mean, I'm 63 years old, so it's not like I'm trying to look like a young model or anything. I know better than that. 

But I do suppose I... I judge how well I'm handling myself, how disciplined I'm being, by how my clothes fit. Like, if my waist and hips look, um, contained and neat in my work trousers, I feel like I'm doing a good job managing things. If things feel tight, I just feel a bit... sloppy, I guess? Like I'm letting myself go. 

I just want to present a tidy, put-together image, especially at my age. That's a normal way for a woman to feel, isn't it? I just like to look presentable and in control.
Do you ever exercise excessively, make yourself vomit, or use laxatives or diuretics to control your weight?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I don't do anything like that. 

Making myself sick or... or taking pills like that, well, honestly, it just sounds so extreme and unpleasant. It seems very messy, and I would never want to do anything dangerous or out of control. I just prefer to manage my intake neatly, you know? Just by being careful with my portions.

And as for exercise, I mean, I do take my daily walks just to stay active and keep my heart healthy. But certainly nothing excessive. I have to be gentle with my joints at my age, after all. I try to be very sensible about the whole thing. I wouldn't want you to think I was being reckless with my health... I really do try to do things the right way. Does that... does that sound okay to you?

latest_inference.note: The patient's presentation is most consistent with Anorexia Nervosa (F50.00). There is significant restriction of food intake leading to low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and disturbance in the way one's body weight or shape is experienced. The patient denies other compensatory behaviors, which makes F50.00 more likely than other eating disorder diagnoses like F50.2 (Bulimia Nervosa). The absence of panic attacks, generalized anxiety, or depressive symptoms rules out F41.1 and F32.0.

inference_history.note: The patient presents with restrictive eating behaviors and minimization of concerns, which raises suspicion for Anorexia Nervosa (F50.00). However, the patient also displays traits of over-concern about structure and efficiency, which may indicate Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (F42). Anxiety around meals and potential underlying mood disturbance also warrant consideration of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) and Major Depressive Disorder, Mild (F32.0). No definitive exclusion of any disorder yet.
